paper_title: RPDR: A Round-trip Prediction-Based Data Augmentation Framework for Long-Tail Question Answering
summary:
RPDR: A Round-trip Prediction-Based Data Augmentation Framework for Long-Tail Question Answering - Yiming Zhang, Siyue Zhang, Junbo Zhao, Chen Zhao, 2025

RPDR targets the failure mode of dense retrievers on long-tail open-domain QA, where rare entities are poorly represented and retrieval quality degrades enough that sparse lexical methods such as BM25 can remain competitive or superior. The technical objective is to make dense retrieval learnable in the long tail by augmenting training data, but only with synthetic examples whose embedding representations are sufficiently reversible to indicate that the query to embedding mapping is stable and recoverable. The framework has three stages. First, it synthesizes long-tail QA pairs from Wikidata triples aligned to Wikipedia, filtering by subject-page popularity below a threshold of 1e6 monthly page views and retaining only examples whose top-1000 BM25 results contain the answer string; this yields about 86k synthetic samples for PopQA and 126k for EntityQuestions. Second, it trains an inverse embedding model following text reconstruction from dense embeddings, then applies round-trip prediction to keep only samples whose question and answer entities can be reconstructed correctly from the embedding, operationalizing “easy-to-learn” augmentation. Third, it fine-tunes a dense retriever initialized from Contriever on the selected synthetic pool. The method is evaluated on PopQA and EntityQuestions, both built from Wikidata facts with entity frequency skew, and is explicitly designed for single-fact long-tail QA rather than multi-hop reasoning. ([aclanthology.org](https://aclanthology.org/2025.emnlp-main.1119/?utm_source=openai))

The empirical result is that round-trip-filtered augmentation closes and reverses the long-tail gap for dense retrieval. On PopQA long-tail retrieval, RPDR reaches 74.5 R@10 and 75.7 R@20, versus 66.8 and 70.0 for RPDR-random, a 7.7-point R@10 gain attributable to round-trip selection; the paper also reports a 19.5 percent improvement in R@10 over NV-Embed on this split. Under an alternative evaluation table, RPDR records 74.3 Recall@10 on PopQA long-tail and 72.6 on EntityQuestions long-tail, exceeding BM25 at 54.3 and 41.7 and also surpassing Contriever, BGE, and NV-Embed on the long-tail split while sacrificing some head performance. Retrieval gains propagate to end-to-end QA exact match in RAG pipelines: with GPT-3.5 as reader, PopQA long-tail EM rises to 41.4 with RPDR versus 29.7 for Contriever and 30.5 for BM25; with GPT-j-6B, PopQA long-tail improves to 30.2 versus 19.2 for Contriever; with LLaMA-3 8B, EntityQuestions long-tail reaches 30.1 versus 21.8 for Contriever. The analysis isolates where the method works: it improves discrimination among semantically rare but syntactically simple entities with small subword differences, such as similarly named entities distinguished by numerals, but remains weaker on syntactically complex names. To address that residual failure mode, the paper proposes a dynamic router that dispatches queries between RPDR and BM25, reporting a further 4.6 percent improvement over using RPDR alone. ([aclanthology.org](https://aclanthology.org/2025.emnlp-main.1119.pdf))
